milestones.title: A connected world of regions
milestones.summary: Several persistent worlds run side by side as one group: Gaia (the mainland), the Rail Yard, Mars and the Moon. Every character has one home world, starts on Gaia and travels to the others in seconds, carrying food, tools and supplies. Sleeping regions wake when a traveller sets off. An Orbit region for space stations follows.
milestones.availability_note: Live on the public server: Gaia, the Rail Yard, Mars and the Moon run as one region group, and the launcher lists and joins every region. The Orbit world is built and goes live next. Travel between groups on different machines is a separate goal below.

evidence.label: Run regions as a group on one host
The Moon as its own world

completion.basis: Maintainer roadmap review on 2026-11-07 accepted the merged implementation as this milestone's scope.

milestones.title: Server updates without a long outage
milestones.summary: A new build is staged beside a running region, loads its save as a standby and takes over while the old world keeps playing. Each region updates in turn, and a failed handover rolls back so play continues on the old build.
milestones.availability_note: Staged handover and its port fixes are merged and can be driven from the launcher. A region's first update onto this build is still an ordinary restart.

evidence.label: Hand a running region over to its staged build
Staged handover ports and launcher view

completion.basis: Maintainer roadmap review on 2026-11-07 accepted the merged implementation as this milestone's scope.

milestones.title: An optional desktop launcher
milestones.summary: The optional Civ13 launcher finds servers, wakes sleeping ones and joins them, and gives hosts a Host tab for every region: start, stop, sleep, wake, save, update with a staged build, advance the shared epoch and run Player help. Direct BYOND joining stays supported.
milestones.availability_note: Per-region host actions, staged updates and epoch control are merged and published in the launcher. New server-management features keep landing in the launcher as they merge.

evidence.label: Save, update and restart each region
One-region host actions and group status

completion.basis: Maintainer roadmap review on 2026-11-07 accepted the merged implementation as this milestone's scope.

milestones.title: Optional Discord sign-in
milestones.summary: Sign in through the launcher with a Discord account so your character can follow your account rather than one BYOND key. Discord stays optional; playing with a BYOND key alone works as before.
milestones.availability_note: Live: Discord sign-in is on by default in the launcher since version 1.4.0, through the public sign-in service.

evidence.label: Discord account keys and join tickets

completion.basis: Maintainer roadmap review on 2026-11-07 accepted the merged implementation as this milestone's scope.

milestones.title: Rockets and space stations in orbit
milestones.summary: Launch into orbit from 1969 with two-stage rockets and capsules, work outside on EVA with handholds and safety tethers, and found a station through a launch complex project, as the starter layout or a station you plan yourself. Every station has a docking airlock: a rocket's crew choose a free port that welcomes them before launch, dock against the hatch and walk aboard, and either side can bar the port. Stations grow with modular pods, extra decks and upkeep, with reusable rockets and wider station networks from 2026.
milestones.availability_note: Merged: orbital flight, EVA, starter stations, module pods and docking, the station designer, and rockets docking at station ports. Docking spacecraft built in orbit firmly to a station is still to come. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Settlements on Mars and the Moon
milestones.summary: Survey other worlds with probes, fly crewed landers, build pressurised habitats with life support, explore in pressure suits, mine ice and regolith, drive sealed rovers and grow self-sufficient bases with a propellant plant and flights home. The Moon opens from 1969 and Mars from 2026.
milestones.availability_note: All six settlement phases are merged, from survey probes to closed-loop bases and return flights.

evidence.label: Closed loops, propellant plant and flights home

completion.basis: Maintainer roadmap review on 2026-11-07 accepted the merged implementation as this milestone's scope.

milestones.title: Aircraft that take off and land
milestones.summary: Build aircraft from parts, taxi down runways and fly over the map, seeing the ground below and casting a shadow. Next: hangars and research so players can build planes, then free-form parts, helicopters and jets, and later air routes, parachutes and weapons.
milestones.availability_note: The flight core and the view from the air are merged; planes are admin-spawned for testing. Hangars and research, which make aircraft available to players, are the next phase.

evidence.label: Ground view, shadows and in-flight saves

milestones.title: Industrialization: factories, pipes and foundries
milestones.summary: Run automated factories with belts, feeder and sorting arms, fabricators and a factory monitor; move liquids through pipe networks with pumps, tanks and reaction vessels; and pour molten metal straight into tools at a casting foundry. Steam-era belts open earlier, and factory arms can load vehicle cargo holds.
milestones.availability_note: Factory automation, chemistry pipelines and the casting foundry are merged. A balance pass on player-built production lines comes later.

completion.basis: Maintainer roadmap review on 2026-11-07 accepted the merged implementation as this milestone's scope.

milestones.title: Metalworking benches and electroplating
milestones.summary: Dedicated weapon, fletching and toolsmith's benches turn materials straight into finished items, and an electroplating bath coats metal objects. More plating metals can follow once those metals exist in the game.
milestones.availability_note: The dedicated benches and the electroplating bath are merged.

completion.basis: Maintainer roadmap review on 2026-11-07 accepted the merged implementation as this milestone's scope.

milestones.title: Map tools for builders
milestones.summary: byond-devtools reads Civ13 maps, renders them as stored or as they look in game with lighting, makes safe copy-on-write edits and previews maps in VS Code. Next: a visual map editor and AI-assisted editing.
milestones.availability_note: The tool foundation is merged in the byond-devtools repository. The visual editor and AI-assisted editing are the next stage.

completion.basis: Maintainer roadmap review on 2026-11-07 accepted the merged implementation as this milestone's scope.

milestones.title: A train home for your party
milestones.summary: Build your party's first train as a project at a railway station whose track runs to the map edge. The finished train waits in its own berth in the Rail Yard world, with party-only doors that raiders can force only while a member is online.
milestones.availability_note: Railway works offices, the Rail Yard world and its berths are merged.

Rail Yard world with party berths

completion.basis: Maintainer roadmap review on 2026-11-07 accepted the merged implementation as this milestone's scope.

milestones.title: The 2026 Digital Age
milestones.summary: A new age after the Modern Age with smartphones, drones, lithium-ion batteries, LED panels, 3D printers and a smart hub that takes voice commands for lights, plugs and locks.
milestones.availability_note: The Digital Age and its first devices are merged.

completion.basis: Maintainer roadmap review on 2026-11-07 accepted the merged implementation as this milestone's scope.

milestones.title: Computers and data networks
milestones.summary: Build computers from swappable parts: a processor, drives, a diskette drive and a printer, each giving the machine new abilities. A 1969 minicomputer runs a command-line OS for writing, printing and copying files. Later ages bring desktops and laptops, wired networks with switches and routers, Wi-Fi, phones as computers, and links between regions through stations players build.
milestones.availability_note: The 1969 minicomputer, its parts and the Files program are merged. Wired networks come next.

milestones.title: Raiders, traders and reputation
milestones.summary: Nomad settlements meet NPC raiding parties and trader caravans, and build a reputation with the groups they deal with.
milestones.availability_note: Raids, caravans and reputation are merged.

completion.basis: Maintainer roadmap review on 2026-11-07 accepted the merged implementation as this milestone's scope.

milestones.title: Wildlife by habitat
milestones.summary: Animals spawn across the whole map according to their habitat instead of fixed spawners that refill on every restart.
milestones.availability_note: Habitat-based wildlife spawning is merged for Nomads maps.

evidence.label: Wildlife by habitat across the map

completion.basis: Maintainer roadmap review on 2026-11-07 accepted the merged implementation as this milestone's scope.

milestones.title: Generated surface, island and cavern worlds
milestones.summary: Generate reproducible surface, ocean-island, cavern and airless worlds from a seed and turn them into playable region maps with resources, wildlife, elevation and climate.
milestones.availability_note: The generators and playable region maps are merged; Mars and the Moon are built this way.

completion.basis: Maintainer roadmap review on 2026-11-07 accepted the merged implementation as this milestone's scope.

milestones.title: Smoother saves for persistent worlds
milestones.summary: Save the world quickly while it keeps running, recover safely after an interrupted save and check the result outside the game so validation never stalls play.
milestones.availability_note: The stream saver, interrupted-save recovery and faster large saves are merged; a full save now takes minutes instead of about twenty. Moving validation into an outside process is the next step.

milestones.title: Extraction survival
milestones.summary: Explore dangerous areas, collect loot and return to a persistent safehouse. Raid worlds such as the Crossroads Mall and the zombie city send persistent characters out and bring them home. Planned for in-game eras from 1943 onward.
milestones.availability_note: Safe houses, the mall raid and raid worlds are merged. Combined persistence, transport and recovery acceptance on a real run remains.

milestones.title: Geography, elevation, realistic weather and the sun
milestones.summary: Biomes, elevation and shelter shape local conditions independently. Mountains are colder, snow builds up without replacing soil, and the sun follows latitude and season, stretching shadows at dawn and dusk. Regions share a calendar but have local time zones and opposite seasons across hemispheres. Weather crosses region boundaries. Climate and air simulation drive pressure, fronts, wind, rain, sleet, snow, freezing rain, hail, fog, dew, frost, wind chill and humid heat. Instruments from bronze rain gauges to modern weather stations help forecast conditions.
milestones.availability_note: Elevation metadata, colder high ground on generated maps, weather-driven snow, and moving sun and shadows are merged. Hand-made maps opting in and real-client checks remain. The shared calendar, time zones and southern seasons, cross-region weather, climate normals, air grid, fronts, wind, precipitation, fog, dew, frost, crop frost covers, feels-like temperature, and instruments by era are also merged. Severe storms can now bring directional gusts and rare land tornadoes with local warnings. See the Weather and Climate wiki guide. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Persistent world editing and map authoring
milestones.summary: Keep zones and spawn points stable through saves and export a saved world back into Civ13 map source for mappers.
milestones.availability_note: Zone persistence and whole-world map export are merged. A visual editor built on byond-devtools and a mapper guide are planned.

evidence.label: Export the whole world as a map

milestones.title: Smooth movement
milestones.summary: Smooth walking, diagonal moves, prone crawling, vendor NPCs and pulling crates and stacks, without changing movement speed or costs.
milestones.availability_note: Player, crawl, vendor and pulling movement are merged and on by default. Smooth wildlife movement remains disabled until its timing is fixed.

milestones.title: Authoritative line of sight
milestones.summary: Walls, doors and openings block what each player can see, applied to hover, examine, targeting and agent observations while the HUD stays visible.
milestones.availability_note: Geometric line of sight, wall faces and opacity refresh are merged. Gameplay adapters, hidden-information protection and cost measurements remain.

milestones.title: Lighting for oversized sprites
milestones.summary: Light large trees, shadows and other artwork that extends beyond its tile, without changing ordinary light propagation.
milestones.availability_note: A disabled composition prototype is merged. Rendering issues and a connected-client check remain.

milestones.title: Liminal Facility escape mode
milestones.summary: A finite escape round through authored rooms, set in 1990, with a threat to avoid, steady lamps and indoor sound.
milestones.availability_note: Room layouts, map export, the escape round and the threat, light and sound pass are merged. Playtesting with real players remains.

milestones.title: Powered-gateway expeditions
milestones.summary: Power a gateway, survey authored rooms with finite supplies and found a persistent colony on the other side.
milestones.availability_note: The design and a disabled power-state foundation are merged. Physical gateways, supplies, rescue and paired-world saves remain.

milestones.title: Diet, preferences and food discovery
milestones.summary: Balanced meals build nutrient reserves and energy, characters learn hidden tastes, and varied recipes pay off.
milestones.availability_note: Balanced diet and hidden tastes are merged. Cave wheat now gives underground farms a year-round grain, and the mild stamina penalty for a long narrow diet is on for the Nomads maps, where every nutrient group can be grown or hunted in every season.

milestones.title: Discord presence, friends and invites
milestones.summary: Show what you are playing on Discord through the launcher, with friends lists, invitations and joining to follow.
milestones.availability_note: Discord activity through the launcher is merged. Friends, invitations and joining are planned.

milestones.title: Player-built crossings and routes
milestones.summary: Players build trail markers that open to another region once an admin approves them, and later ferries and rail routes between regions.
milestones.availability_note: Admin-approved trail markers are merged. Player-made ferries and rail routes between regions are planned.

milestones.title: Jet airstrikes you can see
milestones.summary: Call in close air support and watch it arrive: jets sweep across the battlefield with their shadows below, missiles streak in on smoke trails and bombs walk along the attack line. A forward air controller on modern battles marks targets with a laser designator, and enemy SAM sites can still shoot the jets down.
milestones.availability_note: Merged: F-16 and Su-25 strikes now draw the jet, its shadow and rocket smoke trails, and every Delta Force operator on Syria carries a laser designator. Still to come: air controllers on more modern battles.

milestones.title: Wild West mounted raids
milestones.summary: Ride into town with your gang. A new Little Creek battle starts the outlaws in the saddle outside town, with loot spread along the main street so the raid is a gallop past the bank and the shops, firing from horseback while the Sheriff's posse mounts up to give chase.
milestones.availability_note: Merged: on Little Creek every outlaw now starts in the saddle at the gang's camp, and galloping horses kick up dust. Still to come: loot spread along the main street and a mounted Sheriff's posse.

milestones.title: The Ides of March
milestones.summary: A new Roman battle in and around the senate house. Caesar and his loyal friends and lictors stand together in white togas while conspirators among the senators draw hidden daggers. Keep Caesar alive and get him out, or strike him down and escape to the Capitol.
milestones.availability_note: Merged: The Ides of March battle, with the Curia of Pompey, Caesar, his lictors and friends against Brutus and the senators, who carry a pugio hidden in a pocket; the conspirators win when Caesar dies. Still to come: senators' striped togas and the lictors' fasces.

milestones.title: Naval broadsides
milestones.summary: Crew a sailing warship with your friends. The ships in the naval battle sail and turn for position, full gun decks are worked by gun crews who sponge, load and run out each cannon, and the captain orders a broadside that fires down the whole side in clouds of powder smoke.
milestones.availability_note: Merged: on the Naval Battle the captain's boatswain's call fires every loaded gun on one side in a ripple, and the new Broadside battle puts two ships under sail that close on each other, lay their guns on the enemy hull and win by sinking or boarding her. Still to come: gun crew drills and splashes for misses.

milestones.title: Helicopter air assault
milestones.summary: Ride a Huey into battle in Vietnam. Squads board a helicopter at base, fly low over the map with a door gunner firing below, and jump out at a landing zone while the helicopter heads back for the next wave. Ground fire can damage it and bring it down.
milestones.availability_note: Merged: on the Vietnam battles a UH-1 Huey waits at the American base; squads board it, pick a landing zone or pop signal smoke, and it flies them in over the treetops, drops them off and flies back for the next squad. Still to come: door gunners who fire and ground fire that can bring it down.

milestones.title: Better cooked dishes: seasonings and garnishes
milestones.summary: Cooking grows past the three pot stews. Season dishes with salt, pepper, dried herbs, vinegar and oils, finish them with garnishes such as fresh mint, pickles, jam or roasted seeds, and cook new dishes on the grill, griddle, oven and fryer. A well-seasoned, garnished dish tastes better, earns a higher meal quality and lifts mood more than plain roasted food.
milestones.availability_note: The groundwork is in: pot stews with three quality tiers (salt seasons the best one), learned tastes, and the herbs, teas, mortar-ground oils, vinegar, pickles and jam from the plant processing work. Seasonings, garnishes and the new dishes are not built yet.

references.label: Groundwork: balanced diet and learned tastes

milestones.title: Travel between servers on different machines
milestones.summary: Extend region travel so characters can move between region groups hosted on different machines, with the same single-owner custody and recovery rules.
milestones.availability_note: Travel works within one host's region group. Groups spanning machines need design and testing.

references.label: Groundwork: travel between regions on one host

milestones.title: Design and build your own ships
milestones.summary: Draw a ship tile by tile on a ship's draught: her floors, deck above, masts, rowing benches, anchors, cabin walls and helm, with her size, cost and speed worked out as you draw. Share designs as codes, copy the lines of a ship you admire, then build her on a slipway on the shore with your crew, piece by piece, and launch her down the ways ready to sail.
milestones.availability_note: Merged: ship’s draughts, ready-made designs, slipway construction and launching. The redesigned window shows in-game pictures and checks ship and submarine designs. Ships can include pumps, steam engines, cannons, torpedo tubes and steel fittings. Draw and hand-build cars, trucks, tanks and planes from a vehicle sheet, or use the automobile workshop or aircraft hangar; the hangar also builds helicopters. Draw crewed airships in the airship designer and build them at the airship yard. See Guide to Boats.

milestones.title: Ocean voyages, offshore rigs and submarines
milestones.summary: Sail between ocean maps, build and maintain offshore oil rigs, and build submarines and underwater habitats with pressure, air and power.
milestones.availability_note: Ocean bridges, boats and a shared air ledger for submarine compartments are groundwork. Routes, depth and the vessels themselves need design.

milestones.title: Recovery when a region goes offline
milestones.summary: Let a player recover their character and belongings into another live region after a shutdown or outage, without duplicating anything.
milestones.availability_note: The home ledger records which region owns each player. Fenced ownership of goods and a recovery path remain.

references.label: Groundwork: one home world per character

milestones.title: Homes, towns and player crafts
milestones.summary: Give players reasons to decorate and keep up their homes and towns. A comfortable, varied, well-kept room lifts mood and lets you wake well rested; walls and floors take limewash, paint and stain; furniture fabric and curtains take dyes. Later steps add woven rugs and tapestries, player-designed pottery and statues, named towns with prosperity tiers that new players can choose to start near, and more crafts such as mosaics and stained glass.
milestones.availability_note: Home comfort, Judge This Room, limewash, paint, stain and dyed furniture fabric are merged, and so are fine placement with Nudge Object, player-designed pottery, and woven rugs and tapestries. More floors to lay are merged as well: redrawn cobblestone, stone, marble and wood floors, terracotta tiles and brick paving, iron plate and grating, flagstone, copper, bronze, lead, glass block, rush matting, obsidian and steel tread plate floors, and pelt rugs. Player-designed chairs, beds and stools with replaceable upholstery are merged, and sleeping in a furnished room banks rested research points. Statues, towns and the later crafts are not built yet.

milestones.title: Tamahagane: steel from iron sand
milestones.summary: Make steel the Japanese way. Iron sand is panned from riverbeds, sifted from beaches or washed out of hillside soil in a washing channel, then fired with charcoal in a single-use clay tatara furnace while bellows blow into it. Breaking the furnace open gives a kera bloom and some pig iron; on an anvil the kera sorts into tamahagane and wrought iron, and tamahagane folds into steel. Japanese Swordsmithing adds the tachi and clay hardening, which gives katana and other Japanese blades a hamon and higher quality.
milestones.availability_note: Iron sand, the tatara, the washing channel, sand washing, the tachi and clay hardening are merged. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Doors, locks, bars and trapdoors
milestones.summary: Finish any door by fitting parts to it instead of picking from a long recipe list. Closers and spring hinges shut doors behind you and wedges hold them open; locks come in key families from wooden pins to machined tumblers, plus seals, hidden catches and combination locks, and the same locks fit chests and closets. Bars, bolts and bracing hold a door from your side. Fire doors keep fire and spreading smoke inside their compartment, windows and shutters open and lock, and trapdoors and hatches close the way between levels. Routes and agent characters only pass doors that would open for them.
milestones.availability_note: Door fittings, locks, bars, fire doors, smoke, opening windows, door features, trapdoors and agent routing are merged. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Bees, honey and beeswax
milestones.summary: Keep bees the way people did through history. Rob wild nests in hollow trees with smoke from a smouldering bundle or a torch, then squeeze the comb for honey and melt the wax into beeswax for candles. Later, keep colonies in log hives, clay hives and straw skeps that you stock by catching spring swarms. A colony needs enough honey left to last the winter, and hives raise the harvest of crops that need insects. In the Industrial era, frame hives come with a honey extractor and a beekeeper's veil and suit, and beeswax goes into sealing wax while honey ferments slowly into mead. Characters can be allergic to stings, or hardened against them.
milestones.availability_note: Wild nests, honey hunting, stings, beeswax candles and the sting and allergy traits are merged, and so are log hives, clay hives, skeps and swarms, and bees now pollinate fruit, beans, cotton and flax. Frame hives with the honey extractor, bellows smoker and nucleus box are merged, and so are the veil and suit, sealing wax for seals and slow-fermenting mead. The honeycomb sprite is redrawn and the whole craft has its own Guide to Beekeeping. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Castle defences and gateway traps
milestones.summary: Make castles worth building and hard to take. Cut arrow slits and gun loops through walls to shoot out from cover, build battlements that shield one side, and heat water, oil, pitch, sand or molten lead to pour through murder holes, machicolations and timber hoardings onto attackers below, or drop stones on them. A tar kiln makes pitch. Gateways get drop trapdoors over staked pits worked from a lever, portcullises that crush whoever they land on, caltrops that lame horses, and ladder forks to push siege ladders off the wall.
milestones.availability_note: Arrow slits, gun loops and battlements, pouring and dropping with the murder hole, machicolations, hoardings and the tar kiln, and the gateway traps are merged, with a Defending a Castle wiki guide. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Multi-storey buildings and towers
milestones.summary: Build upward and downward on every persistent land. Each roof adds a floor above, four underground levels lie under every map, and you can see down through open air. Taller buildings need stronger supports and foundations: wood carries two storeys, stone four, and concrete walls and pillars six, so a concrete tower on a proper foundation rises six storeys with a roof terrace on top. Every floor earns its place: cellars stay cool and keep food, mice and floods never reach the rooms upstairs, lofts dry food faster, a chimney carries the hearth's warmth up to the bedrooms, lifts and ramps carry people and goods between floors, railings keep people from walking off balconies, a quiet upstairs bedroom adds comfort, and from the roof you can shoot down and send smoke signals further.
milestones.availability_note: Upper storeys with foundations and support rules, seeing down through open air, floors over upper-floor gaps, and six-storey concrete towers are merged. Every land allows ten levels above ground; supports for storeys seven to ten are not built yet. Four underground levels under every map get slower to dig and richer in ores. Stairs down from upper floors, cellars, lofts, shooting down, upstairs bedrooms, rooftop signals, chimneys, lifts, ramps, stair loads, railings and gates are also merged. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Knowledge that spreads
milestones.summary: Old knowledge no longer stays locked up with whoever found it first. Every subject is guarded, spreading or common knowledge, by how many ages it is behind the world's age. The newest two ages stay guarded and are learned as before. Subjects two or three ages behind are spreading: their chapters take half as long to read or hear, a teacher can show you the whole subject by hand, and researching them again goes three times as fast. Subjects four or more ages behind are common knowledge that every character knows, so someone arriving in an advanced world no longer starts with nothing. Using a subject's things and living around them also teaches a little of it, slowly and never the whole subject on its own.
milestones.availability_note: The three states and their labels in the tech tree are merged, and so are common knowledge for new and living characters, quicker reading and whole-subject teaching of spreading subjects and faster research of them at a bench, and learning a little from using and living around things. The Books and Scholars guide explains it. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Late ages built on scarce materials
milestones.summary: Reaching the later ages takes the materials of the wider world, not only time at a bench. Every age discovery from steam power on, and the biggest late subjects such as rocketry, missiles and orbital flight, needs a bill of materials delivered to the research bench with its book: coal and iron for steam, rubber and zinc for electricity, steel, rubber, lead, sulphur and saltpeter for the World Wars, uranium for nuclear power, and aluminium, gold, silver and gems for computing and spaceflight. Many of these come mostly from particular lands, so trading or holding land abroad is the practical way to the top, although any faction can still do every part itself.
milestones.availability_note: Bills for every age discovery from Steam Power on and for six big late subjects are merged, and the World War II discoveries no longer accept a single part. The Books and Scholars guide explains it. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Languages that grow apart
milestones.summary: Languages can change over a long time, the way Latin became French and Spanish, but only for nations cut off from everyone else. When a nation's native speakers hear nobody but each other, their speech slowly drifts away; any regular contact with other nations pulls it back. A nation that stays drifted and isolated for a week of real time becomes ready to split, and its leader names the new language. Its speakers keep the old one, speakers of the old language follow most of the new one, and it writes in the same script. A language that stays isolated again grows further from its parent, and travellers carry new languages to other lands.
milestones.availability_note: Drift tracking for each nation's speech community is merged, and so are splits after long isolation, Name Our Language, saving and travel, and a Language families view in Check Known Languages. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Peoples that grow from the world
milestones.summary: Peoples are living groups of this world rather than fixed real-world labels. Looks come from where you were born, never from your people, and nobody can see your people on sight. Gaia has peoples of its own. New characters are born into the people of the community they start in. A nation that stays out of touch with every other faction for a long time becomes a people of its own, peoples living together in one nation grow a people of both, and someone who lives among another people can be welcomed by its leader. Nations' leaders name new peoples, and no game rule ever depends on a character's people.
milestones.availability_note: Looks apart from peoples, peoples as world records and Gaia's own peoples, birth into a community, splits after long isolation, blends and belonging and the Your people view in Check Known Languages are merged, and the Peoples and Languages guide explains them. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Holding land on the continents
milestones.summary: Factions compete to hold the continents, which are divided into provinces along coasts, rivers and mountains. Members who live and play there give their side stake, and the side that leads a province for three days holds it. Recruitment stations work only in provinces your side holds, and a bed start after death costs more. A claimed island stays yours unless you leave it empty. A held province's seat ranks from Camp to City, pays weekly upkeep and can be besieged in its daily defence window. Each continent is rich in its own ores, with rich provinces whose seams never run out. Rubber grows only in the jungles of Africa and Asia, land oil flows only on Africa's desert ground, the Americas can frack at a cost to their land, and crops grow faster on Gaia.
milestones.availability_note: Provinces, stake and the Province Holdings view, station rules, the bed start cost, claimed islands, continent resources (including Earth Asia), settlement ranks, upkeep and ruins, sieges, rich provinces across lands, land oil, Gaia crops, Americas fracking and rubber trees are merged. The Civilizations and Nomads, Resource Extraction and Farming guides explain them. Station rules start three weeks after a world first counts stake. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Armor that fits its purpose
milestones.summary: Armor protects by how it is built and what it is made of, never by which culture it looks like. Hits are cuts, thrusts or blows: padding stops blows and arrows, leather turns cuts, lamellar stops arrows, mail stops cuts, and plate stops most things but is heavy. Maces bruise through armor and wear it down, spears find the gaps in mail and lamellar, a padded jack goes under other armor, and no armor recipe ever goes out of date. From the Imperial age a steel proof cuirass turns musket balls, and in the First World War a resin body shield, the Dayfield and a heavy rifle-proof Dayfield are made from resin laminate and steel.
milestones.availability_note: Hit kinds, armor kinds and materials, weapon roles, the padded jack, the examine lines and armor against guns are merged. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Resins, silk and modern fabrics
milestones.summary: Players tap pines for resin and trees for lacquer, raise silkworms for silk, and coat cloth into tarred canvas, oilcloth, waxed cloth and rubberised cloth that shed rain. Spirit varnish brushes a finish that slows wear. Later the bakelizer cooks phenolic resin for pressed resin laminate and spins nylon thread for nylon cloth, epoxy binds glass cloth into fiberglass and aramid laminate, and a resin 3D printer prints parts from photopolymer resin. Resin laminate and steel make the First World War body armor.
milestones.availability_note: The resin materials work is merged, with the wiki guide Resins, Silk & Fabrics. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Nation governments
milestones.summary: Nations choose how they are ruled: a confederation of equal factions, a theocracy, monarchy or dictatorship ruled by one person, or a republic, democracy or merchant league that votes and elects its head for a term. Each has trade-offs in how many factions it holds, who admits members and how long leaving takes. Heads who stay away lose their seat to an heir, a deputy or an election, and citizens can overthrow any government by petition and by holding a nation assembly. Next: tying nation laws and courts to the government, then offices of state and treaties between nations.
milestones.availability_note: Government types, citizen votes and elections, succession, revolts and staff tools are merged, and the Civilizations and Nomads guide explains them. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Accolades and extra characters
milestones.summary: Lifetime achievements that belong to your account rather than one character. Each of 26 accolades, from finishing the tutorial to surviving a long winter, founding a faction or judging at court, is claimed once ever and gives lifetime points. Spend them to unlock up to three more characters, so you can play someone new without giving up the one you have. Switching happens from your character's own bed, and extra characters need a Discord-verified account. An account's characters are publicly known as kin, share one leadership seat, and share province limits, and staff break up any group split into factions to get around claim limits.
milestones.availability_note: Accolades and the Accolades window, characters saved per slot, the Characters window and switching, kin, one leadership seat, shared province caps, court marks on kin, the Magistrate accolade and staff bloc tools, and the staff account lookup are merged, with a Guide to Accolades and Characters. Not yet checked in a live game.

milestones.title: Growing and trading drugs
milestones.summary: Tobacco, opium poppies, coca, cannabis and the new khat shrub grow wild and on farms only in their real climates, so the people who grow them are rarely the people who want them. Lance poppies for opium, chew coca with wood ash, brew poppy and coca tea, rub hashish and chew fresh khat before it wilts. Doctors mix laudanum and refine morphine and cocaine, and heroin comes with modern medicine. Purity depends on the maker's skill, and paper twists hide how strong they are until tasted. Every drug has a real use and a real danger: habits by drug class, tolerance and relapse, deadly overdoses and mixes, and lasting organ damage. Factions allow, license or ban each kind of drug on their land, and trade is between players only.
milestones.availability_note: Wild crops and real climates, drug classes with tolerance, mixing and lasting harm, traditional preparations and khat, apothecary refining and paper twists and faction substance rules are merged, with a Guide to Drugs and Stimulants on the wiki. Not yet checked in a live game.
